Incident INC-1042: AtlasArm Actuator Overheating
# Incident INC-1042: AtlasArm Actuator Overheating

- Reported: September 2024
- Product: AtlasArm industrial arm
- Sites affected: two customer plants (45-unit installed base)
- Severity: major

## Root cause

AeroGrip actuator housings from batch A-2231, machined on Kestrel Metals line 4 in August 2024,
received improper thread-lock application. Sustained load caused the housings to overheat.

## Remediation

- Replace all batch A-2231 housings in the field (completed November 2024).
- Supplier corrective action (CAPA) opened with Kestrel Metals; quality contact Rosa Delgado.
- Quarterly audits of Kestrel machining lines by Priya Nair's quality team.

Warranty treatment followed policy WP-9: actuators carry 18 months of coverage.

AtlasArm industrial arm.

- Motor windings: wound in-house at the Fremont plant.

## Quality history

thread-lock application, causing overheating under sustained load. The issue was tracked as
incident INC-1042 and remediated by replacing affected housings and a supplier corrective action.

Incident INC-1077: NimbusOne Fleet Telemetry Dropouts
# Incident INC-1077: NimbusOne Fleet Telemetry Dropouts

- Reported: May 2024
- Product: NimbusOne delivery drone (1,200 unit fleet, 14 cities)
- Severity: major, no crashes

## Root cause

SkyLink X2 firmware 2.3.1 contained a watchdog reset defect that dropped the telemetry link under
sustained airframe vibration. Average outage per flight was 17 minutes.

## Remediation

- Fleet-wide upgrade to signed firmware 2.3.2 completed June 2024.
- The signed image satisfies security standard SEC-14; compliance audited quarterly by Marcus
  Webb's firmware team.
- Incident owned by Marcus Webb (Firmware Lead).

NimbusOne Delivery Drone
# NimbusOne Delivery Drone

NimbusOne is Nimbus Robotics' flagship autonomous delivery drone, released in March 2024.
It carries a 5 kg payload with a 32 km operating range. The fleet of 1,200 units serves 14 cities.

## Bill of materials highlights

- Telemetry radio: SkyLink X2 module (firmware line 2.x) built by BlueFin Circuits.
- Battery pack: four VoltCore 4000 lithium-ion cells manufactured by Helix Cell Works.
- Final assembly plant: Fremont, CA.

## Service notes

Mid-flight telemetry dropouts observed across the fleet in May 2024 were tracked under incident
INC-1077 and resolved by a signed firmware upgrade. Battery warranty coverage follows policy WP-9.

Standard SEC-14: Firmware Security
# Standard SEC-14: Firmware Security

SEC-14 requires that all field-deployed radios and controllers run cryptographically signed
firmware. Unsigned images and rollbacks below the signed baseline are prohibited.

## Scope

- SkyLink X2 telemetry radio line (NimbusOne, HaloDock links).
- HaloDock dock controllers.

## Compliance

Firmware releases such as SkyLink X2 2.3.2 ship signed images and satisfy SEC-14. Compliance is
audited quarterly by Marcus Webb's firmware team.

SkyLink X2 Radio Module
# SkyLink X2 Radio Module

The SkyLink X2 is a dual-band 2.4/5 GHz telemetry radio module manufactured by BlueFin Circuits.
It is used in the NimbusOne drone and in HaloDock dock controllers.

## Firmware history

- 2.3.0 (February 2024): initial production firmware.
- 2.3.1 (April 2024): introduced a watchdog reset defect causing intermittent link drops under
  sustained vibration; implicated in fleet incident INC-1077.
- 2.3.2 (June 2024): fixes the watchdog reset bug and ships cryptographically signed images,
  satisfying the SEC-14 signed-firmware security standard.

Firmware is distributed through the secure OTA channel only.

Remediation was a fleet‑wide upgrade to signed firmware 2.3.2 completed June 2024, meeting security standard SEC-14 with quarterly compliance audits. The incident was owned by Marcus Webb, Firmware Lead, whose team performed the audit and rollout.

NimbusOne Delivery Drone

Incident INC-1090: HaloDock Breaker Trips
# Incident INC-1090: HaloDock Breaker Trips

- Reported: February 2025
- Product: HaloDock charging dock (900 W)
- Sites affected: three depots
- Severity: moderate

## Root cause

The revision-A 20 A power relay supplied by BlueFin Circuits is undersized for full 900 W
simultaneous charge sessions, tripping depot breakers.

## Remediation

- Interim: dock firmware 3.1 scheduler staggers simultaneous sessions.
- Permanent: 30 A revision-B relay from BlueFin Circuits, depot retrofit in progress.
- Field rollout coordinated by Lena Ortiz (Field Service Manager) with the Hardware Platform
  team.

HaloDock Wireless Charging Dock
# HaloDock Wireless Charging Dock

HaloDock is a wireless charging dock for the NimbusOne drone, released in January 2025 with a
900 W output. Approximately 300 depots operate HaloDock stations.

## Key subsystems

- Power relay: a 20 A relay supplied by BlueFin Circuits (revision A).
- Enclosure: fabricated by Kestrel Metals.
- Load balancing: requires dock firmware 3.1 or later to stagger simultaneous charge sessions.

## Known constraints

Early revision-A relays can trip depot breakers under full 900 W simultaneous load; see incident
INC-1090 for remediation status. Dock controllers fall under the signed-firmware rule SEC-14.

BlueFin Circuits
# BlueFin Circuits

BlueFin Circuits is an electronics manufacturer supplying printed circuit boards and
electromechanical parts to Nimbus Robotics.

## Supplied parts

- SkyLink X2 radio module (complete module build) for NimbusOne and HaloDock.
- AtlasArm controller PCB.
- HaloDock power relay, 20 A, revision A.

## Quality history

The revision-A 20 A relay is undersized for full 900 W simultaneous dock loads; breakers tripped
at three depots in February 2025 under incident INC-1090. A 30 A revision-B relay is scheduled as
the permanent fix. The SkyLink X2 firmware 2.3.1 watchdog defect (incident INC-1077) was also on
BlueFin-built hardware and fixed in signed firmware 2.3.2.

Incident INC-1090: HaloDock Breaker Trips
Incident INC-1090: HaloDock Breaker Trips

Interim remediation applied firmware 3.1 scheduler to stagger sessions; permanent fix will replace relays with 30 A revision‑B units from BlueFin, with depot retrofits underway. Field rollout is led by Lena Ortiz, Field Service Manager, together with the Hardware Platform team.

BlueFin Circuits
BlueFin Circuits

BlueFin Circuits, an electronics manufacturer, supplies printed circuit boards and electromechanical parts to Nimbus Robotics, including the SkyLink X2 radio module (used in NimbusOne and HaloDock), the AtlasArm controller PCB, and a 20 A revision‑A HaloDock power relay. The revision‑A relay was undersized for 900 W dock loads, causing breaker trips at three depots in February 2025 (incident INC‑1090); a 30 A revision‑B relay is slated as the permanent fix. The SkyLink X2 firmware 2.3.1 had a watchdog defect (incident INC‑1077) on BlueFin‑built hardware, corrected with signed firmware 2.3.2.

HaloDock Wireless Charging Dock
HaloDock Wireless Charging Dock

HaloDock Wireless Charging Dock, released Jan 2025, provides 900 W wireless charging for NimbusOne drones; ~300 depots host stations. Key subsystems include a 20 A power relay (BlueFin Circuits, rev A), an enclosure made by Kestrel Metals, and load‑balancing firmware (dock firmware 3.1+). Early rev‑A relays may trip depot breakers under full load (incident INC-1090) and dock controllers are subject to signed‑firmware rule SEC‑14.

# BlueFin Circuits

BlueFin Circuits is an electronics manufacturer supplying printed circuit boards and
electromechanical parts to Nimbus Robotics.

## Supplied parts

- SkyLink X2 radio module (complete module build) for NimbusOne and HaloDock.
- AtlasArm controller PCB.
- HaloDock power relay, 20 A, revision A.

## Quality history

The revision-A 20 A relay is undersized for full 900 W simultaneous dock loads; breakers tripped
at three depots in February 2025 under incident INC-1090. A 30 A revision-B relay is scheduled as
the permanent fix. The SkyLink X2 firmware 2.3.1 watchdog defect (incident INC-1077) was also on
BlueFin-built hardware and fixed in signed firmware 2.3.2.

Incident INC-1042: AtlasArm Actuator Overheating
# Incident INC-1042: AtlasArm Actuator Overheating

- Reported: September 2024
- Product: AtlasArm industrial arm
- Sites affected: two customer plants (45-unit installed base)
- Severity: major

## Root cause

AeroGrip actuator housings from batch A-2231, machined on Kestrel Metals line 4 in August 2024,
received improper thread-lock application. Sustained load caused the housings to overheat.

## Remediation

- Replace all batch A-2231 housings in the field (completed November 2024).
- Supplier corrective action (CAPA) opened with Kestrel Metals; quality contact Rosa Delgado.
- Quarterly audits of Kestrel machining lines by Priya Nair's quality team.

Warranty treatment followed policy WP-9: actuators carry 18 months of coverage.
